subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of covectors in the basis dx^β
subproblems.statement:
For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n:
α = Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β,
where I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P is the finite type of order embeddings β : Fin n ↪o Fin P, α(e_β) = euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(e_{β(0)},…,e_{β(n−1)}) with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and dx^β = wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n), α = ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β • wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: this child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge of DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.covector_expansion-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 6c6b4b2753e8214a3e45619bb0b65d8d553557a5, isolated comparator "Your solution is okay!", no dependencies). Its frozen Lean type, title and statement are copied byte-for-byte from that node. The proof below is that node's accepted proof, copied verbatim; inside it, "the parent" and "the parent proof" mean root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1, not deformation_skeleton_polyhedral. Use in deformation_skeleton_polyhedral: the "Coordinate fact" of the Conventions (α = Σ_γ α(e_γ)dx^γ, hence w(α) = Σ_γ α(e_γ)w^γ); (T2), "writing ω = Σ_γ ω_γdx^γ"; Step 8, "with α′ = dx^γ for every γ ∈ I(n,d) (coordinate fact)": an n-vector that vanishes on every dx^γ is 0 (kernel-checked consequence SkelGlueV2.nvector_ext).

Source: Fact A in the parent proof's conventions (an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}), proved here in full.

Notation:
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
- For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P, e_v := (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}).
- I(n,P) := SimonMultiIndex n P = Fin n ↪o Fin P, a finite type.
- For β ∈ I(n,P), α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. (Kronecker property.) Let β, γ ∈ I(n,P). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} = proj(β(i))(e_{γ(j)}) is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.
(a) If β = γ, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j (β is injective). So M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1.
(b) If β ≠ γ, there is i with β(i) ∉ {γ(0),…,γ(n−1)}. Otherwise range β ⊆ range γ. Both ranges have exactly n elements because β and γ are injective (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), so range β = range γ (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le). An order embedding of the well-order Fin n is determined by its range (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so β = γ, a contradiction. For this i, row i of M is zero, hence det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
Thus dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.
2. (Agreement on increasing tuples.) Let R := Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β, a continuous alternating n-linear map. For γ ∈ I(n,P), Step 1 gives R(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·δ_{βγ} = α(e_γ).
3. (Agreement on injective tuples.) Let v : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n with v∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). Since v∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := v∘σ defines an element of I(n,P) (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono) with e_γ = e_v∘σ. For every alternating map f, f(e_v∘σ) = sign(σ)·f(e_v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Applying this to α and to R and using Step 2 gives sign(σ)·α(e_v) = α(e_γ) = R(e_γ) = sign(σ)·R(e_v). Acting with sign(σ)⁻¹ (inv_smul_smul) yields α(e_v) = R(e_v).
4. (Conclusion.) Two alternating multilinear maps on ℝ^P that agree on all tuples (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis). Hence α and R are equal as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
5. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–4 cover them. For n = 0, I(0,P) has one element, dx^β is the constant covector 1, and the identity reads α = α(())·1. For n > P, I(n,P) is empty, so R = 0, and no injective v exists, so Step 4 gives α = 0 = R. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^β(e_γ) = det[δ_{β(i)γ(j)}] = δ_{βγ} for increasing β, γ.
R := Σ_β α(e_β)dx^β agrees with α on increasing basis tuples.
Sorting an injective tuple (Tuple.sort, AlternatingMap.map_perm) gives agreement on all injective basis tuples.
Module.Basis.ext_alternating gives α = R.

subproblems.title: Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| for test forms supported in W
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C

The proof below is that node's accepted proof, copied verbatim; inside it, "the parent" and "the parent proof" mean root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1, not deformation_skeleton_polyhedral. Use in deformation_skeleton_polyhedral: (T1) "|Q(ω)| ≤ μ_Q(W)‖ω‖ if tsupport ω ⊆ W (same for ∂Q)", combined with M_W(Y) = μ(W ∩ A) from deformation_mass_restriction (kernel-checked: SkelGlueV2.mass_bound_use); (T2) "M(∂p_γ#(X⌞ω_γ)) ≤ M_W(∂X)|ω_γ| + M_W(X)|dω_γ|"; (T3) "|Y(g dy)| ≤ M_W(Y)‖g‖" and "|Y(∂_jg dy)| ≤ M_W(∂Y)‖g‖"; Step 4(c) "|Y_F(g du)| ≤ μ_Q(tube)‖g‖" and Step 4(d) "|∂Y_F(φ)| ≤ μ_∂(tube)‖φ‖".

Source: parent proof Step 2 (basic mass estimate). It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: |tα| = |t|·|α| and C ≥ 0.
For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of an n-dimensional coordinate box in ℝ^N
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, let α : Fin n ↪o Fin N be a strictly increasing multi-index with range A := range α, let c : Fin N → ℝ and let a ≤ b be real numbers. Let B := {x ∈ ℝ^N : c_i + a ≤ x_i ≤ c_i + b for i ∈ A, and x_i = c_i for i ∉ A}. Then μHE[n](B) = (b − a)^n, where μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N (equal to Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n); the equality is stated in [0, ∞] as μHE[n](B) = ENNReal.ofReal((b − a)^n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (α : SimonMultiIndex n N) (c : Fin N → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), a ≤ b → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl N)) {x : Eucl N | ∀ i : Fin N, (i ∈ range α → c i + a ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ c i + b) ∧ (i ∉ range α → x i = c i)} = ENNReal.ofReal ((b - a) ^ n)

The bound enters (T5) (|P(ω)| ≤ (Σ_{F∩tsupport ω≠∅}|β_F|)‖ω‖) and Step 6 (M(P) ≤ Σ_F|β_F|M([[F]]) ≤ 2M(Q)).

Source: step 7 of the parent proof ("Measures of faces"), stated for an arbitrary base point c and bounds a ≤ b. With c_i = ρ z_i it gives μHE[n](latticeFace ρ (z, α)) = ρ^n for (a, b) = (0, ρ) (valid as ρ ≥ 0) and μHE[n](K_δ) = (ρ(1 − 2δ))^n for (a, b) = (ρδ, ρ(1 − δ)). Notation: A := range α, B := the set in the statement, x_i := the i-th coordinate of x ∈ ℝ^N.

1. Parametrization. Define ι : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ^N by ι(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ c_i + Σ_{j ∈ Fin n} [α(j) = i] · y_j), where [α(j) = i] is 1 if α(j) = i and 0 otherwise. Because α is injective, for j ∈ Fin n exactly one summand of ι(y)_{α(j)} survives, so ι(y)_{α(j)} = c_{α(j)} + y_j; for i ∉ A every summand vanishes, so ι(y)_i = c_i.
2. ι is an isometry. Let y, y' ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). By `EuclideanSpace.dist_eq`, dist(ι y, ι y') = sqrt(Σ_{i ∈ Fin N} dist(ι(y)_i, ι(y')_i)²) and dist(y, y') = sqrt(Σ_{j ∈ Fin n} dist(y_j, y'_j)²). In the first sum each term with i ∉ A vanishes (both coordinates equal c_i), so the sum equals the sum over the image α(Fin n) (`Finset.sum_subset`); reindexing along the injective α (`Finset.sum_image`) it becomes Σ_j dist(c_{α(j)} + y_j, c_{α(j)} + y'_j)² = Σ_j dist(y_j, y'_j)² (`dist_add_left`). Hence dist(ι y, ι y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y', i.e. ι is an isometry (`Isometry.of_dist_eq`).
3. ι maps the cube onto B. Let Q := {y ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) : a ≤ y_j ≤ b for all j}. (⊆) Let y ∈ Q. For i = α(j) ∈ A, ι(y)_i = c_i + y_j ∈ [c_i + a, c_i + b]; for i ∉ A, ι(y)_i = c_i. So ι(y) ∈ B. (⊇) Let x ∈ B and define y ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) by y_j := x_{α(j)} − c_{α(j)}. Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P carries its Borel σ-algebra, μ is any measure on it, and μ⌞A = `μ.restrict A`. For a Borel set B, μ⌞B(E) = μ(E ∩ B) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`); for a Borel set E, μ⌞A(E) = μ(E ∩ A) for every A (`Measure.restrict_apply`). 'μ-null-measurable' means measurable for the completion of μ (`NullMeasurableSet A μ`).

1. (Borel kernel.) Since A is μ-null-measurable, there is a Borel set A′ ⊆ A with A′ = A μ-almost everywhere (Mathlib `NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`). In particular μ(A ∖ A′) = 0.

2. (Finite pieces.) Since μ⌞A is σ-finite, there are Borel sets S_m (m ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_m S_m = ℝ^P and μ⌞A(S_m) < ∞ for every m (Mathlib `spanningSets (μ.restrict A)` with `measurableSet_spanningSets`, `measure_spanningSets_lt_top`, `iUnion_spanningSets`). Put B_m := A′ ∩ S_m; it is a Borel set. Since B_m ⊆ A′ ⊆ A, we have B_m ∩ A = B_m, hence μ(B_m) = μ(B_m ∩ A) = μ⌞A(B_m) ≤ μ⌞A(S_m) < ∞.

3. (Inner regularity on one finite piece.) Fix m and put ν_m := μ⌞B_m, so ν_m(E) = μ(E ∩ B_m) for every E. Then ν_m(ℝ^P) = μ(B_m) < ∞, so ν_m is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P. Since ℝ^P is a σ-compact metric space, every locally finite (in particular every finite) Borel measure on ℝ^P is regular (Mathlib `Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure`; classically Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2) with Remarks 1.16 and 1.12, or Ulam's tightness theorem for finite Borel measures on Polish spaces). In particular ν_m is inner regular with respect to compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure (Mathlib: `Regular` gives `InnerRegularCompactLTTop`, and then `MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt`, whose remaining hypotheses hold because ℝ^P is Hausdorff and its Borel σ-algebra contains the open sets). Applying this to the Borel set B_m, which has ν_m(B_m) = μ(B_m) < ∞, gives for every j ∈ ℕ a compact set K_{m,j} ⊆ B_m with ν_m(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1). As B_m ∖ K_{m,j} ⊆ B_m, ν_m(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) = μ((B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) ∩ B_m) = μ(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}). Hence μ(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1) for all m, j ∈ ℕ.

4. (Null remainder in each piece.) Fix m. For every j, B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′} ⊆ B_m ∖ K_{m,j}, so by monotonicity and step 3, μ(B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′}) < 1/(j+1). Letting j → ∞ gives μ(B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′}) = 0.

5. (Global remainder.) Let x ∈ A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}. If x ∉ A′, then x ∈ A ∖ A′. If x ∈ A′, choose m with x ∈ S_m (the S_m cover ℝ^P); then x ∈ B_m and x ∉ ⋃_j K_{m,j}, so x ∈ B_m ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}. Hence A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j} ⊆ (A ∖ A′) ∪ ⋃_m (B_m ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}). By monotonicity and countable subadditivity, together with steps 1 and 4, μ(A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}) = 0.

6. (Re-indexing.) Let k ↦ (a(k), b(k)) := Nat.unpair k, a surjection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ because Nat.unpair (Nat.pair m j) = (m, j). Put C_k := K_{a(k), b(k)}. Each C_k is compact, and C_k ⊆ B_{a(k)} ⊆ A′ ⊆ A. By surjectivity, ⋃_k C_k = ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}. Step 5 then gives μ(A ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. ∎

σ-finiteness of μ⌞A gives Borel S_m covering ℝ^P with μ(A′ ∩ S_m) = μ⌞A(A′ ∩ S_m) < ∞.

Statement. Let n ∈ ℕ, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support, and q ∈ ℕ. Proof. We prove a more general claim by induction on q, in which the kernel may be vector-valued; this is needed because the derivative of a real kernel is vector-valued.

1. (General convolutions.) For real normed spaces E, F (F complete), a continuous bilinear map L : E × ℝ → F (Lean: L : E →L[ℝ] ℝ →L[ℝ] F), a function f : ℝⁿ → E and g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), put (f ∗_L g)(x) := ∫ L(f(t), g(x − t)) dt (Lean: convolution f g L volume). For E = F = ℝ and L = lsmul (L(s, t) = s t) this is φ ∗ g.

2. (Claim P(q).) For all E, F, L as in 1 and every B ≥ 0 with ‖L(u, t)‖ ≤ B ‖u‖ |t| for all u ∈ E, t ∈ ℝ; every C^∞ f : ℝⁿ → E with compact support; every S ∈ ℝ with ‖D^q f(t)‖ ≤ S for all t; every g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) and every x ∈ ℝⁿ:
 ‖D^q(f ∗_L g)(x)‖ ≤ B · S · ∫ |g| dLⁿ.
(The bound is phrased with an explicit constant B rather than the operator norm ‖L‖; this avoids norm-instance issues for the iterated bilinear maps of Step 4 and is mathematically equivalent.)

3. (P(0).) D^0 h(x) is h(x) (up to the isometry identifying E with 0-multilinear maps; `norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero`). By `convolution_def` and the norm bound for integrals (`norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`): ‖(f ∗_L g)(x)‖ ≤ ∫ ‖L(f(t), g(x − t))‖ dt ≤ ∫ B S |g(x − t)| dt = B S ∫ |g(x − t)| dt = B S ∫ |g| dLⁿ, since ‖f(t)‖ ≤ S and Lebesgue measure is invariant under t ↦ x − t (`integral_sub_left_eq_self`; t ↦ |g(x − t)| is integrable by `Integrable.comp_sub_left`).

4. (Derivative of a convolution.) If f is C^∞ with compact support and g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) (in particular locally integrable), then f ∗_L g is differentiable at every point with D(f ∗_L g)(y) = ((Df) ∗_{L'} g)(y) (differentiation under the integral sign; Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left`), where Df : ℝⁿ → (ℝⁿ →L E) is again C^∞ with compact support (`ContDiff.fderiv_right`, `HasCompactSupport.fderiv`) and L' := L.precompL : (ℝⁿ →L E) × ℝ → (ℝⁿ →L F), L'(u, t)(v) = L(u v, t). Hence, as functions, D(f ∗_L g) = (Df) ∗_{L'} g.

5. (P(q) ⇒ P(q + 1).) Let f, S be as in P(q+1), i.e. ‖D^{q+1} f(t)‖ ≤ S for all t. The (q+1)-st derivative is the q-th derivative of the first derivative, with equal norms: ‖D^{q+1}h(x)‖ = ‖D^q(Dh)(x)‖ (Mathlib `norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv`).  ‖D^{q+1}(f ∗_L g)(x)‖ = ‖D^q((Df) ∗_{L'} g)(x)‖ ≤ B · S · ∫|g| dLⁿ

For the plane itself, η_{x,r}(Π_F) = span e_α for x ∈ Π_F, so the blow-up integrals are constant in r and the tangent space of (Π_F, |β_F|) at x is span e_α, which has dimension n.

Source: the locality step (P5)(iv)/(P3) of the parent proof (“the weighted approximate tangent space at x only depends on M, θ near x, modulo Hᵏ-null sets; for small r the blow-up integrals only see x + r·spt f ⊆ V, and Hᵏ(η_{x,r}Z) = r^{−k}Hᵏ(Z) = 0 for null Z”), written out against the frozen definition `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt` (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7). This argument has been kernel-checked against the frozen definitions (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only).

Notation. H := Hᵏ = `μHE[k]` on ℝ^P. For r > 0, η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (`blowUpMap x r`). By definition, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L` means: dim L = k (`finrank ℝ L = k`), and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dH as r ↓ 0 (limit along 𝓝[>]0).

1. (Null sets under blow-up.) If r > 0 and H(Z) = 0 then H(η_r(Z)) = 0. Indeed |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹ and μH[k](η_r(Z)) ≤ r^{−k}μH[k](Z) (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`). Moreover H = c_k·μH[k] with c_k ∈ (0,∞) (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H(Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](η_r(Z)) = 0 ⇒ H(η_r(Z)) = 0.
2. (Elementary facts on η_r.) For r > 0, η_r is a bijection of ℝ^P with inverse y ↦ x + ry. Hence η_r(A ∩ B) = η_r(A) ∩ η_r(B), η_r(A ∖ B) = η_r(A) ∖ η_r(B) for all A, B, and η_r(V) = {y : x + ry ∈ V} is open (preimage of the open V under a continuous map).
3. (Reduction.) The dimension conditions for (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) are the same condition on L. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ). Choose R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded), and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V open, x ∈ V). We prove I_{M,θ}(r) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) for every r ∈ (0, δ/R). Since (0, δ/R) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the two functions of r agree eventually as r ↓ 0, so I_{M′,θ′}(r) has the same limit θ(x)∫_L f dH, which equals θ′(x)∫_L f dH because θ(x) = θ′(x). This gives `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M′ θ′ x L`.
4. (Integrands vanish off η_r(V).) Let r ∈ (0, δ/R), g : ℝ^P → ℝ arbitrary, F_g(y) := f(y)g(x + ry). If y ∉ η_r(V) then x + ry ∉ V ⊇ B_δ(x), so r|y| ≥ δ, hence |y| ≥ δ/r > R, f(y) = 0 and F_g(y) = 0.
5. (Step A: cutting by V.) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P and every g: ∫_{η_r(S)} F_g dH = ∫_{η_r(S∩V)} F_g dH. Indeed η_r(S ∩ V) = η_r(S) ∩ η_r(V) (step 2); since η_r(V) is open (measurable), H⌞(η_r(V) ∩ η_r(S)) = (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) (`Measure.restrict_restrict`); and the integral of F_g with respect to (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) equals its integral with respect to H⌞η_r(S), because F_g vanishes off η_r(V) (step 4; `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero`).
6. (Step C: replacing θ by θ′.) ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_θ dH = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_{θ′} dH. By hypothesis (H⌞(M∩V)){z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} = 0, so there is a Borel set N ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} with (H⌞(M∩V))(N) = H(N ∩ (M∩V)) = 0 (`exists_measurable_superset_of_null`, `Measure.restrict_apply`). Let N′ := {y : x + ry ∈ N}, a Borel set. Then {y : F_θ(y) ≠ F_{θ′}(y)} ⊆ N′, and N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V) ⊆ η_r(N ∩ (M∩V)) (if y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M ∩ V and x + ry = z ∈ N). By step 1 the right side is H-null, so (H⌞η_r(M∩V))(N′) = H(N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V)) = 0; thus F_θ = F_{θ′} (H⌞η_r(M∩V))-a.e. and the integrals agree (`integral_congr_ae`).
7. (Step B: replacing M by M′.) η_r(M∩V) and η_r(M′∩V) are H-a.e. equal sets: by step 2 their differences are η_r((M∩V)∖(M′∩V)) and η_r((M′∩V)∖(M∩V)), both contained in η_r((M Δ M′) ∩ V), which is H-null by the hypothesis H((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 and step 1. Hence H⌞η_r(M∩V) = H⌞η_r(M′∩V) (`ae_eq_set`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`).
8. (Conclusion.) For r ∈ (0, δ/R): I_{M,θ}(r) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_θ dH (step 5) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 6) = ∫_{η_r(M′∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 7) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) (step 5 applied to M′, θ′). By step 3 the lemma is proved. No measurability of M, M′, θ, θ′ is used.
proof_key_steps: Blow-up maps η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) are Lipschitz, so they map Hᵏ-null sets to Hᵏ-null sets.
Choose R with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and δ with B_δ(x) ⊆ V; for r < δ/R the blow-up integrands vanish off the open set η_r(V).
Hence each blow-up integral over η_r(S) equals the one over η_r(S ∩ V).
On η_r(M ∩ V) the weights θ(x+r·) and θ′(x+r·) agree a.e., and η_r(M∩V), η_r(M′∩V) are a.e. equal.
The blow-up integrals of (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) coincide for all small r and θ(x) = θ′(x), so the limits and hence the weighted tangent spaces agree.

subproblems.title: Simple n-vectors: Gram-determinant norm and change of frame (parent P1)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n and every family v = (v₁,…,v_n) in ℝ^P, the operator norm of the simple n-vector simpleNVector v (the functional α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n) on n-covectors, which carry the multilinear operator norm) satisfies ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}; and for every real n×n matrix B and every τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P, simpleNVector(i ↦ Σ_j B_ij τ_j) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ.

Use in deformation_skeleton_polyhedral: the "Unit fact" of the Conventions, the orientation clause of IsRectifiableTriple, and Step 8, "Taking Euclidean norms (|ξ′| = 1 a.e. on M′, |simpleNVector e_α| = 1)". The first conjunct gives ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det I = 1 for orthonormal τ, so ‖±simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 in the operator norm of NVector (kernel-checked: SkelGlueV2.simple_unit, and SkelGlueV2.face_frame_unit for e_α). Step 8 only takes norms of both sides of θ′ξ′1_{M′} = (θ_F∘ι_F⁻¹)·simpleNVector(e_α)·1_{F̊}. It needs only a norm in which these unit n-vectors have norm 1, so it holds verbatim with this norm: θ′1_{M′} = |θ_F∘ι_F⁻¹|1_{F̊} λ-a.e.

Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

Throughout, G(v) := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is the Gram matrix of v = (v₁,…,v_n) and, for a real n×n matrix B and τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n), (Bτ)_i := Σ_j B_ij τ_j. This is item (P1) of the parent proof.

1. (Second identity: change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector. By multilinearity,
 α(Bτ) = Σ_{g : Fin n → Fin n} (Π_i B_{i g(i)}) · α(τ_{g(1)}, …, τ_{g(n)}).
 If g is not injective two arguments coincide and the term vanishes because α is alternating. If g = σ is a permutation, α(τ∘σ) = sign(σ) α(τ). Hence α(Bτ) = (Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_i B_{iσ(i)}) α(τ) = det(B) α(τ) by the Leibniz formula (det B = det Bᵀ, so the row/column convention is immaterial). As this holds for every α, simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B) • simpleNVector τ. For n = 0 both sides are the functional α ↦ α(∅) and the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.

2. (Gram matrices transform by congruence.) G(Bτ)_{ik} = ⟨Σ_j B_ij τ_j, Σ_l B_kl τ_l⟩ = (B G(τ) Bᵀ)_{ik}; hence det G(Bτ) = det(B)² det G(τ).

3. (Upper bound for orthonormal families.) If τ is orthonormal then |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|τ_i| = ‖α‖ for every α, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ 1.

4. (Lower bound for orthonormal families.) Let τ be orthonormal (n ≥ 1), W := span τ and π_W the orthogonal projection onto W. Define α₀(u₁,…,u_n) := det(⟨u_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear and alternating (a determinant whose i-th row depends linearly on u_i, and two equal u's give two equal rows) and continuous (finite dimension). The i-th row (⟨u_i,τ_j⟩)_j is the coordinate vector of π_W u_i in the orthonormal basis τ, of Euclidean length |π_W u_i| ≤ |u_i|. By Hadamard's inequality |det A| ≤ Π_i |row_i(A)| (proof: if the rows are dependent det A = 0; otherwise Gram–Schmidt on the rows gives A = R O with O orthogonal and R lower triangular with diagonal entries |a_i^⊥| ≤ |a_i|, a_i^⊥ the component of the i-th row orthogonal to the previous rows, so |det A| = Π|a_i^⊥| ≤ Π|a_i|; in Lean this is `Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le` for the volume form of W composed with π_W) we get |α₀(u)| ≤ Π|u_i|, i.e. ‖α₀‖ ≤ 1. Since α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det I = 1, ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≥ |simpleNVector τ (α₀)| / ‖α₀‖ ≥ 1. Together with step 3: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 = det G(τ). For n = 0, 0-covectors are the constants c = α(∅) with ‖α‖ = |c|, so ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1 = det of the empty matrix.

5. (Dependent families.) If v₁,…,v_n are linearly dependent then α(v) = 0 for every alternating α (`AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent`), so simpleNVector v = 0 and ‖simpleNVector v‖² = 0. Also G(v) is singular: for a nontrivial c with Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 we get G(v)c = (⟨v_i, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩)_i = 0, so det G(v) = 0. The first identity holds. (This covers in particular n > P.)

6. (Independent families.) If v is linearly independent, Gram–Schmidt produces an orthonormal τ with span τ = span v and v = Bτ, B_ij = ⟨v_i, τ_j⟩, B invertible. By step 1, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector τ, so by step 4, ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B|. By step 2 and G(τ) = I, det G(v) = det(B)². Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det G(v) = det (Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨v_i, v_j⟩).

Steps 5–6 give the first conjunct for every v; step 1 gives the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Leibniz expansion and the alternating property give α(Bτ) = det(B)·α(τ) for every n-covector α, hence simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B)•simpleNVector τ.
Gram matrices transform by congruence: det G(Bτ) = det(B)²·det G(τ).
For orthonormal τ: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π|τ_i| = 1, and the covector det(⟨u_i,τ_j⟩) has norm ≤ 1 by Hadamard and value 1 at τ, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
Dependent families: simpleNVector v = 0 and det G(v) = 0.
Independent families: Gram–Schmidt v = Bτ gives ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B| and det G(v) = det(B)².

subproblems.title: Antilipschitz charts pull back Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ and c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 we have Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the estimate of step 1 of the parent proof: Ψ = (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ is (1/c)-Lipschitz, so it maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ(Ω) to Lⁿ-null sets (Lⁿ(Ψ(Z)) ≤ c^{−n} Hⁿ(Z)).

1. Φ is injective on Ω: if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω then c|w − w′| ≤ 0, so |w − w′| = 0 since c > 0.
2. If Ω = ∅, then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise ℝⁿ is nonempty and Ψ := Function.invFunOn Φ Ω satisfies Ψ(Φ(w)) = w for all w ∈ Ω (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn).
3. Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω): for y = Φ(w), y′ = Φ(w′) with w, w′ ∈ Ω, |Ψ(y) − Ψ(y′)| = |w − w′| ≤ c⁻¹|Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| = c⁻¹|y − y′| (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul with constant Real.toNNReal c⁻¹).

Lipschitz maps increase Hⁿ by at most the n-th power of the constant (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, scaled by the normalizing factor of μHE[n]; packaged as SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, which is in scope): Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)) ≤ (c⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

Ψ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(Ω).
Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) ⊆ Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω)).
Hⁿ Lipschitz image bound (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn) gives Hⁿ(Ψ(Z ∩ Φ(Ω))) = 0.
Lⁿ = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ concludes.
